Build the next population with NSGA-II environmental selection

Source: R/RcppExports.R
replacement_cpp.Rd

The num_to_replace best offspring (by NSGA-II rank and crowding distance) replace the lowest-quality parents, keeping the best population_size - num_to_replace parents. This preserves elitism while letting offspring enter only on merit. If num_to_replace <= 0 the population is unchanged.

Usage

replacement_cpp(
  population,
  offspring,
  fitness,
  offspring_fitness,
  num_to_replace
)

Arguments

population

Numeric matrix of current individuals.

offspring

Numeric matrix of offspring.

fitness

Numeric matrix of current population fitness scores.

offspring_fitness

Numeric matrix of offspring fitness scores.

num_to_replace

Maximum number of offspring to admit.

Value

Numeric matrix of the updated population.

See also

initialize_population_cpp(), evaluate_fitness_cpp(), selection_cpp(), crossover_cpp(), mutation_cpp(), bioga_main_cpp()

Examples

genomic_data <- matrix(rnorm(100), nrow = 10, ncol = 10)
population <- BioGA::initialize_population_cpp(genomic_data, population_size = 5)
fitness <- BioGA::evaluate_fitness_cpp(genomic_data, population, c(1.0, 0.5))
offspring <- population
offspring_fitness <- fitness
BioGA::replacement_cpp(population, offspring, fitness, offspring_fitness,
  num_to_replace = 1)
